Thanks Paul — that clarifies a lot. A few technical constraints / recommendations from the Redwood runtime side:

- Egress model: we strongly prefer preserving source IPs for traceability (pods -> external services). Per-rack eBGP is ideal for us; that lets us advertise cluster prefixes and rely on fabric ACLs for multi-tenant guardrails. If BlueCedar insists on a NAT pool, we need predictable SNAT mapping ranges and a fallback path for capacity spikes.

- PV model: recommended mapping:
  * ephemeral NVMe/local SSD = /var/tmp/cache and for model shard caching only (no long-term state)
  * blockstore (iSCSI/LUN) = postgres, logs, customer data volumes (LUKS encrypted; we integrate with Vault via a wrap-unwrap flow)
  * object storage (S3 compatible) = large model checkpoints, immutable artifacts (we will prefer streaming to avoid large PVs)

- Node pools: propose three initial node classes:
  1) cpu-standard (8-16 vCPU, 64-128GB RAM) 
  2) gpu-inference (A10/A100 class, 1-4 GPUs) with taints gpu=true:NoSchedule
  3) storage-heavy (4-8 vCPU, 256-2TB NVMe or blockstore attachment) for persistent DB and job runners

Eviction / QoS: set model-serving pods to Guaranteed where possible; use pod disruption budgets for critical replicas. For storage-heavy node pools, configure node-level retention and eviction thresholds at 80% disk to avoid noisy-neighbor IO storms.

- Monitoring / CNI: we need eBPF-level visibility for prefix-level NAT and to correlate pod IP -> egress mappings. Recommend CNI that supports native eBPF such as Cilium.

I'll prepare a short decision matrix showing tradeoffs and a proposed default mapping for PV classes to avoid back-and-forth on the handoff day.

Karthik
Principal Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — summarizing decisions and next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

Decisions (agreed):
- Egress: BlueCedar will provide per-rack eBGP sessions to the ToR and advertise cluster prefixes. Redwood will not SNAT by default; we will preserve pod source IPs.
